text: Around 11.5 million workers in Viet Nam, roughly one in five workers, are in occupations with tasks potentially exposed to GenAI.
Fewer than 2% of workers in Viet Nam are in occupations where tasks are both highly susceptible to GenAI and standardized enough to imply higher full-automation risk.
The empirical evidence reviewed by ILO shows limited large-scale job displacement so far, despite real and uneven productivity gains.
The evidence reviewed by ILO identifies erosion of employment opportunities for younger workers as an important emerging risk.
BLS projects U.S. software developer employment to increase 10.2% from 2025 to 2035, adding about 174,700 jobs.
BLS projects U.S. computer programmer employment to decline 7.3% from 2025 to 2035, a decrease of about 8,100 jobs.
Execution-heavy programming roles appear more exposed to automation pressure than broader software development roles that include design, integration and system responsibility.
notes: Inference from occupation definitions and divergent BLS projections; not a causal estimate of AI alone.

text: Across 38 countries in the OECD Skills for Jobs 2026 database, persistent shortages are concentrated in high-skilled occupations, especially ICT, health and teaching professionals.
OECD reports that shortages of ICT professionals in the United States intensified after the 2022 launch of ChatGPT.
notes: OECD describes the association; this does not establish that ChatGPT caused the shortage.

text: Across 40 million online job postings in 19 Asian economies, employer demand fell by nearly 10% in more AI-exposed occupations relative to less-exposed occupations.
IMF finds that the relative decline in employer demand for more AI-exposed occupations appears to have stabilized even as AI capabilities continued to improve.
IMF reports rising demand for workers with AI skills in Asian job postings.
Entry-level pathways should be tracked separately from total occupational employment because task automation can weaken the route into a profession before the profession itself contracts.
notes: Career-planning inference supported by youth-risk and hiring-demand evidence; not yet a universal labor-market law.
